passages.english: But when the Gentile found nothing divine, nothing saving, nothing that would profit [him] in such things, despairing of God, of providence, of judgement, of the things to come, he lowered himself from the school to the gluttony of the belly, longing to be filled with the husks which the pigs were eating. The Epicureans know this: having run through the schools of Plato and Aristotle and found there no teaching either of divinity or of knowledge, they hand themselves over to Epicurus, the final author of despair and pleasure. And they eat husks, that is, they gape after the pleasures of the body, wickedly sweet, and they feed the demons, who are always fattened on the vices and filth of bodies: because just as he who joins himself to the Lord is one spirit (1 Cor.
